skill.name: reactivation-specialist
skill.description: Design closed-loop reactivation programs for lapsed email subscribers. Use it to define inactive cohorts, build offer ladders, capture re-consent, and set suppression rules. It does not send campaigns, store consent records, or compute SEND audit scores.
skill.summary: Builds win-back, re-permission, and sunset plans for lapsed email cohorts.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

content.value_statement: Lapsed subscribers reduce deliverability and create consent uncertainty. This skill builds a staged win-back, re-consent, and suppression plan.
actual_capabilities: Defines a lapsed cohort using a no-open or no-click window.
Designs a staged offer ladder with timing, triggers, and stop rules.
Adds a re-consent step that requires a confirming action.
Sets a terminal rule for re-permission or suppression.
Creates a handoff summary for consent and SEND nurture owners.
limitations: It does not send messages or call ESP APIs by itself.
It does not store legal consent records; it hands facts to consent-registry.
It does not calculate EQS or enforce auditor vetoes.
It needs a cohort window or enough context to infer one.

use_cases.title: Recover inactive buyers
use_cases.description: Build a controlled win-back ladder for customers who stopped opening or clicking.

use_cases.title: Run a re-permission sweep
use_cases.description: Ask inactive contacts to confirm consent before moving non-responders to suppression.

use_cases.title: Clean a stale newsletter list
use_cases.description: Separate recoverable readers from contacts that should be sunset or suppressed.

prompt_templates.title: Basic win-back plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known inactive window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic win-back plan for subscribers with no opens in 120 days. My ESP is Mailchimp and I can offer 15 percent off.

prompt_templates.title: Re-permission sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a re-permission sequence for a retention newsletter. Use three touches, include a click-to-confirm step, and define the suppression rule.

prompt_templates.title: Export-informed ladder
prompt_templates.scenario: Use available engagement data with clear evidence labels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this lapsed cohort export summary and design an offer ladder. Use measured values where present and mark missing data as estimated.

prompt_templates.title: Closed-loop program
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced plan with handoffs and terminal states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a closed-loop reactivation program for a 180-day inactive segment. Include cohort definition, offer ladder, re-consent capture, sunset-confirm rule, and handoff summary.

output_examples.input: No clicks in 180 days, 12,000 contacts, and a 10 percent discount available.
output: Cohort: no click in 180 days, excluding suppressed and bounced contacts.
Ladder: soft reminder, conditional discount, final notice.
Terminal rule: confirm consent to return, or move to suppression after no response.

output_examples.input: Need re-permission for a newsletter audience with missing export data.
output_examples.output: The skill would mark cohort size as Estimated, set a three-touch sequence, require confirmation click, and list exports as open loops.

output_examples.input: Complaints are rising among old subscribers and I need to reduce risk.
output_examples.output: The skill would cap sends, exclude suppressed contacts, add a last-chance notice, and hand suppression outcomes to consent-registry.

best_practices: Exclude hard-bounced, unsubscribed, and suppressed contacts before building the lapsed cohort.
Cap the full ladder to three or four touches and stop after the final notice.
Record re-consent and suppression outcomes in the consent registry handoff.
anti_patterns: Do not keep retrying inactive subscribers after the last-chance step.
Do not treat an email open alone as renewed permission.
Do not enroll contacts when consent status is unknown.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails automatically?
faq.answer: No. It designs the reactivation program and handoff summary. Sending remains under your ESP workflow.

faq.question: Can it use ESP engagement exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use user-provided export summaries and labels measured, user-provided, or estimated data.

faq.question: Does it replace the consent registry?
faq.answer: No. It defines the capture step, then hands consent and suppression facts to the registry owner.

faq.question: Does it calculate SEND EQS?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the program and facts for the email-quality-auditor to score.

faq.question: What inputs are most useful?
faq.answer: Provide the inactivity window, ESP name, cohort size, engagement recency, complaint signals, and available incentive.

faq.question: Can it work without an incentive?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build a ladder with a soft reminder, re-consent action, and last-chance notice.
